title: Why Every AI Says 27 When You Ask for a Random Number
topic: LLM 'random' numbers: models copy the numbers humans call random (27/37/73 in ranges, 7 in 1-10)
audience: Anyone who has used ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude; people who like testing AI
whyCare: Viewers can test it in 10 seconds on their own AI and compare answers with friends; the surprise is that 'random' is a copied human habit.

evidence.claim: Press (OfficeChai, The Register June 2025): ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Llama all answer 27 for 'random number 1 to 50'; widely shared on Reddit/X, multi-language coverage through 2026 (73 variant for 1-100)

Paper: Coronado-Blazquez, 'Deterministic or probabilistic? The psychology of LLMs as random number generators' arXiv 2502.19965: 1-10 -> 7 about 80% for several models; 1-100 -> 37/47/73; bigger models not less biased
Humans do the same: about a third pick 7 in 1-10 (YouGov/Hill, secondary), Veritasium 1-100 study favours numbers containing 7 (via arXiv paper)

gap: Existing tech catalogue (62 videos, checked 2026-11-03) has no random-number video; neighbours: sycophancy, hangman, strawberry (different mechanism).
angle: Frame 0: 50-tile grid, scanner racing, locks on 27. Mechanism: AI predicts the most common human answer, it does not roll dice. Payoff: it mirrors human 'random'. Fix: make it run code.
send_reason: Send to a friend with 'ask your AI for a random number 1-50, what did you get?'
